newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs end mostly up, pork bellies pare gains.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs end mostly up, pork bellies pare gains.

text.p: CME hog futures eased from best levels late but finished mostly higher while pork bellies finsihed higher but under best levels, traders said.
Hog futures finished 0.300 cent lower to 0.600 higher with only February off at 75.450 cents. Pork bellies ended 0.850 to 0.125 higher paced by February at 75.050 cents.

Profit-taking pared best levels in both pits after the early short-covering rally. February hogs remained under pressure from expected further losses in cash hogs now that the weather has turned warmer and hogs backed up by the cold start coming to market, traders said.

However, much of the warmer weather's effect on the market was already in the market and this prompted short-covering in February early. Deferred months remained supported by the recent bullish Hogs and Pigs in December which showed reduced hog supplies into this year, they added.

Lind-Waldock, RBH and Rand Financials bought February on the early recovery after scattered initial pressure. Demand was mixed in back months. ADM Investor Services offered February 74 put options early while general bidding was cited in 76 to 80 calls, pit sources said.

Pork belly futures remained supported by short-covering prompted by an oversold condition and expectations that Tuesday's monthly USDA Cold Storage report will show frozen belly stocks below year-ago levels, traders said.

Analyst estimates on the USDA monthly U.S. Cold Storage report pointed to total U.S. frozen belly stocks at between 37.4 to 41.5 million lbs. This compares with 30.9 million on hand December 1 and 47.6 million in storage January 1, 1996.
Report ideas also offset expectations of increased hog slaughter this week, they said.
Iowa Grain was a notable buyer of February early, pit sources said.
Futures closed early at noon CST in observance of the Martin Luther King Jr holiday.
